recent_articles.title: Twisha Sharma death: Madhya Pradesh DGP defends Bhopal Police as CBI takes over case, launches probe - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Madhya Pradesh** Director General of Police (DGP) Kailash Makwana stated that the **Bhopal Police** followed established procedures in the Twisha Sharma death case, which was subsequently taken over by the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**.  The family has alleged institutional bias and procedural lapses by local police, including accusations against retired district judge Giribala Singh, who is an accused in the dowry death and harassment case. The CBI team visited Ms. Singh's residence and questioned her while also meeting with the victim’s family members. The **High Court** will hear petitions challenging Ms. Singh’s anticipatory bail on May 27th.

recent_articles.title: Indigenous Vayu Astra-1 completes high-altitude trials in Uttarakhand, Pokhran - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nibe Limited**, a Pune-based defense technology firm, successfully completed no-cost, no-commitment demonstrations of its indigenous loitering munition system ‘Vayu Astra-1’ for the **Indian Army**. The demonstrations were conducted in April at Pokhran in Rajasthan and Joshimath (Malari) in Uttarakhand.  The anti-personnel variant of Vayu Astra-1 demonstrated a 10-kg warhead strike at a range of 100 km with a CEP of less than one meter, achieving an abort attack and reattack capability during the trials.

recent_articles.title: Centre tells Supreme Court no new hydel projects should come up in upper Ganga - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union government** has submitted to the Supreme Court that no new hydroelectric projects should be permitted in the upper reaches of the Ganga in Uttarakhand. The Ministries of Environment, Jal Shakti and Power presented a single affidavit stating this position, citing concerns about cumulative impact on the ecosystem and seismic fragility. This decision comes after years of expert recommendations and court orders regarding dam development's potential to exacerbate flooding risks.  The matter is scheduled for hearing on May 20th.

recent_articles.title: Uttarakhand files first FIR on allegations of nikah halala under Uniform Civil Code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Uttarakhand Police** have filed a chargesheet in an alleged nikah halala case, invoking provisions of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) alongside dowry and Muslim marriage laws. The FIR, registered on April 4th, 2026, was initially based on allegations of dowry harassment, cruelty, and violations of Muslim marriage laws.  The investigation later included examination of nikah halala allegations, leading to the addition of UCC-linked provisions in the chargesheet. **Nine** accused were named in the final report, with notices issued under the BNSS provisions.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Congress slams Modi Government over women’s safety citing NCRB data - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** party leaders, including **Mallikarjun Kharge**, criticized the **Narendra Modi Government** for its handling of women's safety and rising crime rates.  Kharge cited data from the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) showing a significant increase in crimes against women, children, Dalits, Adivasis, and cybercrime during the past decade. He accused the government of using "Beti Bachao" and "Nari Vandan" as mere slogans while failing to address these issues effectively. **Alka Lamba**, president of the All India Mahila Congress, echoed these concerns, alleging that the BJP was shielding perpetrators instead of ensuring justice for victims.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: PM Modi on West Bengal election result: ‘Lotus’ is blooming from Gangotri to Gangasagar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** praised the outcomes of the elections in four States and a Union Territory as a triumph of democracy and the Constitution, attributing the BJP's success to voters seeking stability and development amidst global turmoil. He highlighted women's crucial role in building a developed India, accusing the Congress and Samajwadi Party of blocking women's reservation in the Lok Sabha.  **Modi** expressed confidence that the BJP-led NDA would continue its efforts to serve people and work ceaselessly for a developed India.

recent_articles.title: Nepal lodges protest against India over long-running border dispute | Border Disputes News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nepal**'s Ministry of Foreign Affairs lodged a protest against **India** after the country announced the resumption of a religious pilgrimage through the Lipulekh Pass, which is claimed by **Nepal** based on a 1816 treaty.  **India** maintains that the pass has been used for pilgrimages since 1954 and disputes **Nepal's** territorial claims. The dispute reignited after **India** agreed with **China** to resume the pilgrimage, which was suspended in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

recent_articles.title: Independent journalism punished, compliance rewarded under current regime, says Kharge - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge** criticized the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** government for its alleged attempts to suppress press freedom in India.  He stated that since 2014, India's position in the World Press Freedom Index has declined and the BJP is seeking to tighten its control over social media to silence dissent. **Kharge** also accused the government of weaponizing legal frameworks to intimidate journalists and noted a sharp rise in arrests and imprisonments of journalists. He highlighted several high-profile cases, including those of journalists murdered while reporting on corruption.  He urged for upholding democratic norms by those in power.

recent_articles.title: India rejects Nepal’s objection to Kailash Manasarovar Yatra via Lipulekh Pass - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** responded to **Nepal's** objection to the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra passing through Lipulekh Pass, stating that such territorial claims are "untenable." The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) clarified that Lipulekh Pass has been a long-standing route for the pilgrimage since 1954 and that India remains open to dialogue with **Nepal** on all bilateral issues.

recent_articles.title: Uttarakhand youth dies by suicide after alleging police harassment in video on social media - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pankaj Kumar**, a 20-year-old from Retpur village, was found hanging from a bridge in Satpuli, Uttarakhand on Saturday.  He had posted a video online accusing **local police** of harassment after seizing his motorcycle. **Police** identified the deceased and informed his family. The incident was reported to authorities by a local resident who alerted them through an emergency call.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: Kailash Mansarovar Yatra 2026: dates, routes, application process and all you need to know - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)** announced the schedule for this year's Kailash Manasarovar Yatra, which will take place between June and August.  A computer-generated, random selection process will be used to select 20 batches of 50 tourists each, with one batch traveling through Uttarakhand via Lipulekh Pass and another through Sikkim via Nathu La Pass.

recent_articles.title: Hindustan Zinc dividend alert! Last date to buy shares for Rs 11 dividend, do you own? - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hindustan Zinc**, a subsidiary of **Vedanta**, announced a 550% interim dividend on its shares, totaling Rs 4,648 crore.  Shareholders who purchased shares before April 30th will be eligible for the dividend, which will be credited to their demat accounts by tomorrow. This latest dividend follows a consistent tradition of rewarding shareholders and brings the company's total dividend payouts since 2001 to 44. The announcement coincided with **Hindustan Zinc**'s Q4 earnings report, which showed a 68% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 5,033 crore for the January-March quarter of FY26.

recent_articles.title: World’s hottest cities: India transforms into a scorching furnace with cities shockingly hitting 46°C | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** heatwave continues to impact multiple cities, with temperatures reaching 46 degrees Celsius in several areas. **The India Meteorological Department (IMD)** has issued warnings about the intense heat, predicting a heatwave in parts of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and central India. The IMD advises citizens to take precautions against heat stress by avoiding sun exposure during peak hours, staying hydrated, wearing loose-fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous activity.

recent_articles.title: NGT issues notice to Centre over risks from hanging glaciers in central Himalaya - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** has ordered responses from various government agencies and organizations regarding the dangers posed by hanging glaciers in central Himalaya. The tribunal, hearing a case based on a newspaper report, found that four researchers from different institutions assessed the potential impact of glacier retreat and instability, concluding that ice avalanches could reach major settlements.  The NGT also noted violations of the Environment (Protection) Act related to these concerns, prompting the inclusion of several government bodies as respondents in the proceedings.

recent_articles.title: Allahabad HC raps U.P. police for ‘disturbing trend’ of harassing young couples - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Allahabad High Court** criticized the **Uttar Pradesh police** for pursuing young couples who have married, instead of focusing on serious crimes. The court found that the police's actions were a violation of personal liberty and quashed an FIR filed by Saharanpur police based on a missing complaint from the woman's father.  The court emphasized adults' right to choose their partners and live independently.

recent_articles.title: Eight killed after vehicle plunges into gorge in Uttarakhand - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Eight people** died and two others were injured when a vehicle carrying them plunged into a deep gorge in Uttarakhand, India on Thursday afternoon. The accident occurred near the Chamba–Koti stretch while the victims were returning home from a cremation.  The **Sub-Divisional Magistrate Alkesh Naudiyal** confirmed that the vehicle fell nearly 300 meters into the gorge.

recent_articles.title: Indian man converted from Hinduism to Christianity denied asylum in Australia; tribunal says no risk of harm on return - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A 23-year-old Indian man who converted to Christianity and sought asylum in Australia was denied refugee status by the **Immigration and Protection Tribunal**. The tribunal found that his claims of persecution from family members were not credible, citing inconsistencies in his account and a lack of attempts to seek help from authorities.  The tribunal also ruled that there was no evidence he would face escalating harm upon returning to India, nor any indication he could not relocate safely within the country.

recent_articles.title: PM inaugurates Delhi-Dehradun expressway - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** inaugurated a six-lane Delhi-Dehradun expressway, a ₹12,000-crore project that is expected to reduce travel time between the two cities. The 213-km corridor will connect key towns in Uttar Pradesh and integrate with major national corridors. **Mr. Modi** highlighted the project's transformative impact on regional connectivity, trade, industry, and tourism.  The project also includes wildlife corridors and amenities for improved safety and access to markets. **Nitin Gadkari**, Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways, emphasized ongoing infrastructure development in Uttarakhand, including projects aimed at improving access to pilgrimage centers.

recent_articles.title: PM inaugurates Delhi-Dehradun expressway - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** inaugurated a six-lane Delhi-Dehradun expressway, a ₹12,000-crore project that aims to reduce travel time between the two cities. The 213-km corridor will significantly improve regional connectivity and integrate with major national corridors. **Mr. Modi** highlighted the government's focus on infrastructure development and its impact on tourism in Uttarakhand, noting a surge in visitor numbers to pilgrimage sites like Adi Kailash and Om Parvat.  Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways **Nitin Gadkari** announced several connectivity projects slated for completion or launch over the next two years, including a four-lane bypass at Rudraprayag and Kashipur, as well as a greenfield corridor between Delhi and Haridwar.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by **West Bengal**, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 12 States and UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which saw a significant reduction in voter numbers across nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by West Bengal with 83.86 lakh.  The revision identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters for removal. The consolidated electoral rolls across these regions saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Uttarakhand police unable to enforce UCC due to delay in software update - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Uttarakhand** police are unable to register cases under sections of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) due to a software update delay on the **Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS)** platform. The issue arose when Shaheen, a resident of Haridwar, filed a complaint against her husband and in-laws alleging dowry harassment and triple talaq.  **Uttarakhand** police have registered an FIR under relevant provisions of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita but are unable to utilize sections of the UCC due to a lack of software updates.

recent_articles.title: Meat shops in Haridwar to be shifted to outskirts ahead of Ardh Kumbh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haridwar Municipal Corporation (HMC)** has approved a proposal to ban the sale of raw meat in the city ahead of the Ardh Kumbh Mela, scheduled from January 14th to Maha Shivratri. The decision will see all meat shops relocated to Sarai village on the outskirts of the city.  The move follows objections from some Congress councillors but was passed by a majority vote from **BJP** councillors. The HMC has also announced registration requirements for residents with more than five dairy animals, including cows and buffaloes.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026: ECI may roll out SIR in remaining 17 States, 5 UTs post polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission** is considering rolling out the third and final phase of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) for voters' lists in 22 states and Union territories after the Assembly elections this month. The exercise, which aims to clean up electoral rolls, could begin after the polls conclude on April 29th or after the declaration of results.  The **Election Commission** has already conducted SIR in 10 states and three Union Territories, covering nearly 60 crore voters.

recent_articles.title: Conversion politics, the challenge to secularism - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Reports** of arrests of Muslims from various backgrounds in North India for alleged involvement in organized networks facilitating religious conversion from Hinduism to Islam have emerged. These cases, predominantly in Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, are under investigation.  Concerns about religious conversion, particularly from Hinduism to Islam, have been a contentious issue in India for decades. The debate has led to the enactment of anti-conversion laws across various states, with some being tightened by BJP-ruled governments. However, these laws have also been criticized for potentially encouraging vigilantism and violence.

recent_articles.title: Uttarakhand Police honoured with the President's Police Colours - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Uttarakhand Police** has been awarded the President's Police Colours, the highest national award for a state police force. The award was presented to **Director General of Police Deepam Seth** by **Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami**, who described it as a significant achievement marking the state's 25th anniversary.  The recognition is based on the police force's efficiency in disaster management, particularly during the 2013 Kedarnath tragedy, and its successful handling of security, traffic, and crowd control during large events like the Maha Kumbh, Char Dham Yatra, and Kanwar Yatra.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027 kicks off: How to do self-enumeration: step-by-step guide - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner will conduct the 2027 census, a massive administrative and statistical exercise that collects demographic data on the entire country. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their household information online before enumerators visit, offering flexibility in filling out the census schedule.  The dates for self-enumeration vary by state and union territory, with most starting in April 2026. Census data is expected to be published within 2027 due to the digital nature of the process.

recent_articles.title: 55,000 households use Census self-enumeration portal on day one - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Droupadi Murmu**, **Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan**, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, and **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** were among the first to use the online self-enumeration portal for the 2027 Population Census in eight States and Union Territories. The portal, which launched on April 1, 2026, allows households to provide information about their housing conditions and assets before enumerators visit.  The first phase of the census, focusing on house listing operations and housing census (HLO), will run until May 15th in these areas. Data collected through self-enumeration is confidential and will be used for evidence-based planning and policy formulation.

recent_articles.title: What is the Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Bill? | Explained - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Maharashtra** government passed the Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Bill, 2026, which aims to prohibit unlawful religious conversions. The bill mandates a 60-day notice period for conversion and requires police registration of complaints related to forced conversions.  Civil society organizations have expressed concerns about the bill's potential impact on personal liberty and its constitutionality.  The bill has been supported by **Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis**, who stated that it is necessary to address increasing cases of forcible religious conversions. The bill has also been criticized for potentially targeting minority communities and raising administrative concerns regarding the lack of a certification system for religions.

recent_articles.title: Amit Shah promises UCC in Assam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, Union Home Minister, stated that the **BJP** would introduce the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in Assam if re-elected for a third consecutive term. The proposed UCC includes a provision to ban polygamy and aims to bring uniformity in civil laws and strengthen social reforms.  **Assam** previously passed an anti-polygamy bill in 2025, seen as a step towards implementing the UCC. **Uttarakhand** was the first state to implement the UCC in 2025.
